solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cops, elite crew endlessly trained for special force

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into shape, so these letters are reworked into a new order
endlessly says the word crew loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Police officers and a crack team, drilled hard, make up a special unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims crew to CRE; 'trained' rearranges COPS + ELITE + CRE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret police is a covert state security service, a special force operating outside the ordinary constabulary.

indicators.note: in a down clue, backing up says the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a smear is a stain or mark

explanation.surface: A US politician supports a colleague while smearing a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to bear its weight or uphold it, a synonym of support used as a verb.

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: roll over is a command, and over here means the list word is turned backwards

parts.note: a rota is a roll or list of duties

explanation.surface: An owner commands a guard dog to perform its trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a command to a pet; 'Guard' is actually the definition, a keeper of a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator looks after a museum collection, acting as its custodian or keeper.

clue.text: Observed government cut by one American state

indicators.note: cut says the word for government loses its last letter

parts.note: an empire is a realm under imperial government
I is the Roman numeral one
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a state government has been trimmed back by a single US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical findings come from observation and experiment, so observed is an adjectival synonym.

indicators.note: in a down clue the royal piece sits under the others, so it comes last

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
OS stands for outsize, meaning huge
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The rock band Queen's song Under Pressure is paired with something enormous to suit a showman.
explanation.walkthrough: Under Pressure is a famous Queen song, but here 'Under' places ER below P + OS.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is someone who shows off to impress others, an exhibitionist in casual use.

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so it comes after

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
a pier is a supporting column or pillar

explanation.surface: A rickety column holds up a toilet, making it ever wobblier.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy means crazy or unbalanced, so the comparative means more mentally unstable.

indicators.note: leading puts the first piece in front of the next
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to race is to hasten or hurry

explanation.surface: A Tory leader moderates his stance at the front of a leadership race.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to restrain or subdue, so it can stand for moderate as a verb.

clue.text: God is pure, men beg to be changed

indicators.note: to be changed asks for the letters of these words to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A preacher says the deity is pure and men must beg to be reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme being is a phrase for the highest divine power, the deity worshipped as creator.

clue.text: A French bit's flipped? Take off!

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: flipped says the word for bits is turned backwards

parts.note: bit's read as bit is, giving PART plus S, the plural word for pieces

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a French part has flipped over and tells it to get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off!' sounds like a dismissal but means remove a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstrap is to undo a buckle and remove the item, such as a watch or harness.

definitions.meaning: to stand something is to tolerate or put up with it
breadbasket is slang for the belly or digestive organ

explanation.definitionFit: To be able to stomach something is to tolerate it, and the belly organ is jokingly a breadbasket.

clue.text: Doctor treats here with case of lolly involved

definitions.text: Doctor treats here with case of lolly involved

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together into one mix, so they are rearranged
the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: A private physician sees patients in an address where plenty of money changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges TREATS HERE with LY, the case of lolly (British slang for money); HARLEY STREET is the London street famous for private medical practices.
explanation.definitionFit: This London street is the famous home of private doctors, so it is literally where a doctor treats patients for money.

clue.text: It generates energy in relation to star perhaps

parts.note: re means regarding or in relation to
a film star is an example of an actor

explanation.surface: A remark about a star being a source of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests a sun generating energy, but it is a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is a plant that produces power by controlled fission.

clue.text: Roll around front of inn and make merry

indicators.note: around says the list word surrounds the other letter

parts.note: a roster is a roll or duty list

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Revellers stagger round outside a pub and celebrate noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel boisterously, enjoying oneself loudly in company.

clue.text: Sound of bird could alert him?

definitions.text: Sound of bird could alert him?

indicators.note: sound of says the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a mynah is a talking bird of the starling family

explanation.surface: A bird's call might serve as a warning to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Canaries were taken down coal mines to warn of gas, so a bird could alert a pit worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit worker in a coal mine was traditionally warned of gas by a caged bird falling silent.

clue.text: Catholic Church containing King with a new sanction

parts.note: Lear is the king in Shakespeare's tragedy
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: The Catholic Church, with royal backing, gives a novel kind of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearance is official permission to proceed, so it is a noun synonym of sanction.

indicators.note: inside says the letters are found within the run of words before it

explanation.surface: Someone wanting a lively pick-me-up drink is told to put ice in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisk and energetic both describe someone moving quickly and with vigour.

clue.text: Game girl who's striking, holding a weapon

indicators.note: holding says the word for a beauty encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a belle is a strikingly beautiful girl
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A stunning young woman carrying a weapon is up for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' suggests violence, but here it means beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game played by striking balls towards pins and holes.

indicators.note: deviant means straying from normal, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A wayward Frenchman proves frosty company.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacial literally means icy, and figuratively describes a cold, unfriendly manner.

clue.text: Tours around outside of course showing muscles

indicators.note: around says the word for tours surrounds the other letters

parts.note: trips are tours or journeys

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tourists walk round a golf course showing off their physiques.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps are the large muscles at the back of the upper arm, a plural-looking muscle name.

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: to ram is to strike forcefully

explanation.surface: A golfer's wood hits the ball, making several shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shots' and 'wood' suggest golf, but shots are measures of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Drams are small measures of whisky, like shots of spirits.

definitions.meaning: unmentionables is a coy word for underwear such as knickers
a chest of ... has sliding compartments, and the query flags the furniture sense of chest

explanation.definitionFit: Drawers is an old word for underpants and also the sliding boxes in a chest of furniture.

parts.note: via means through or by way of

indicators.note: almost says the word for experiment loses its final letter

parts.note: a test is an experiment

explanation.surface: An amateur, by trial and error, nearly gets off the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot an aircraft, so aviates is a third-person synonym of flies.

clue.text: Fancy one compiler concealing a trap

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: concealing says the setter's pronoun hides the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the compiler, the setter, refers to himself as me
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: A crossword setter keeps a trap hidden away, which is a fanciful idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy is to suppose or picture something, a verb synonym of imagine.

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A player is told to abide by the rules of tennis at all times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow' seems to mean obey the rules, but it means come after.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards as a result, so it means follow.

parts.note: suggests a crook stitched up for a crime, but describes a tradesman fitting panes into window frames

explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits panes of glass sets them into frames, so his work is framed.

definitions.meaning: Guinea is a West African country, with the possessive added
these were British gold coins worth 21 shillings, still used in horse racing

explanation.definitionFit: The West African state's name with a possessive gives this word, also the plural of an old British coin worth 21 shillings.

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity's admirers send letters of encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan letters' reads as mail from admirers; 'Fan' is a verb rearranging the word letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a supporting frame, two pairs of legs holding up a table top.

clue.text: Copies produced initially by art classes, mixed taking time

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word is taken
taking says the jumbled letters enclose the time abbreviation
mixed says the letters of these words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Art students make replicas of sculptures over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts T inside LASERCASTS, the anagram of ART CLASSES from 'mixed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster casts are replicas made by pouring plaster into a mould of an original sculpture.
